static_traits.name: Yang Kexin
static_traits.occupation: University student currently studying (career not yet decided)
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate (currently in university, once dropped out to care for grandparents, later re-enrolled)
static_traits.family_status: Living with parents and a young sibling
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with classmates due to math pressure, collaboration affected; has a supportive family but not yet fully disclosed the predicament to family
static_traits.medical_history: No prior psychotherapy/counseling experience; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Steady speech rate, clear expression; able to self-Reflect, cooperative Good; tense emotions, Self-denial and 'should'-style statements present

basic_info.main_problem: I struggle with mathematics and feel I will most likely fail the course.
basic_info.core_demands: Because fear of failure in mathematics and persistent pressure affect overall physical and mental well-being and daily life, seeking support and guidance to relieve pressure and improve their state.
growth_experiences: Once dropped out of university to care for grandparents, a major life turning point; after re-enrolling feels disconnected from the past self, viewing High school achievements as 'another person's life'. This experience makes maladjustment and Self-doubt more likely in university Learning.

Always had difficulties with math in the past, but never as overwhelming as now; this long-standing weak subject was significantly amplified upon entering more complex content, further intensifying failure Anticipation and Anxiety.

Good grades in the High school stage formed the inner standard 'I should stay excellent'; when unable to reach past levels at the current university stage, tends to interpret this as 'failure', reinforcing Self-denial and Sense of frustration.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough / not competent enough.

special_situations.event: Whenever facing math homework or exams
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot quickly understand complex math content, it means I am not smart enough and will eventually fail the course.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling Learning efforts, asking classmates for help, using online resources, trying deep breathing in exams to control Anxiety.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail the course; I am not smart enough.

special_situations.event: When starting to answer questions in a major exam of the most difficult course
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform poorly in key exams, it proves I am simply not suited for university Learning.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism after exams, reducing interaction with others, tending toward Withdrawal to avoid further exposing inadequacy.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My mind is blank; I am bound to fail.

special_situations.event: When comparing current university performance with high High school grades
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If current levels do not reach past ones, it equals failure, meaning I am no longer excellent.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constant self-comparison and self-reproach, trying to 'prove oneself' through harder Learning.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as before, so I am a failure.

special_situations.event: When cooperating with classmates to complete homework, needing collaborative communication
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not do well enough, others will surely see me as holding them back.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces interaction, avoids proactive cooperation to lower the risk of being evaluated.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me, seeing me as a burden.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as capable, able to handle university studies, and gaining recognition and acceptance.
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure, negation, and shame; worrying about exposing the 'not smart enough' side and being judged.
defense_goal: Reducing failure Anxiety through overexerted Learning and rationalized control
Avoiding or Withdrawing in high-pressure scenarios to escape judgment and setbacks

object_relations.self_representation: Not smart enough, a Student possibly holding others back
object_relations.object_representation: Picky classmates and teachers with high standards

object_relations.self_representation: Not wanting family to worry, a child holding on
object_relations.object_representation: Supportive family who may not understand the real predicament

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited by the counselor to observe and record thoughts, or to discuss the theme of 'comparison and shoulds'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands the counseling process as a task of needing to use rationality to 'collect evidence' to control the emotions, vaguely regarding the counselor as someone evaluating his ability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Steady tone, mainly analysis and logic, frequently using 'evidence/reason' vocabulary; when invited to touch emotions, turning back to discussing 'what should be done'.

manifestations: Relationship tension with classmates and teachers due to persistent failure Anticipation and Self-denial, cooperation affected
Not yet fully expressing the real predicament to supportive family, feeling distant from others
outcomes: Decreased self-confidence, Anxiety and Repression intensified
Withdrawing in academics and relationships, further solidifying the 'I am not good enough' self-schema

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Repeatedly judging oneself by the inner standard 'I should perform better like in High school'
Demanding oneself with the rigid rule that failing a course equals failure

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Turning pressure and unease into self-reproach and Self-denial
Reducing communication in cooperative settings, showing Withdrawal and even the impulse to drop out again

positive_force: Family support exists, has potential social support resources
Good High school grades, with some Learning ability and methodological foundation
Willing to try recording observations and behavioral experiments, higher willingness to cooperate
Has proactively sought help (classmates, online resources), with help-seeking awareness
Still tries to 'push through' tasks under pressure, has a certain perseverance
negative_force: Cognitive biases of catastrophizing and predicting the future (e.g. 'I will fail the course')
Ongoing comparison with past achievements leading to Self-denial (Comparing and Despairing)
High Anxiety in Exam settings with mind-body reactions (mind going blank)
Avoidance and Withdrawal tendencies (reducing cooperation, wanting to drop out)
Not yet fully expressing the predicament to family, not yet effectively mobilizing external support

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic Anticipation and strong Anxiety before and after math assignments and exams, with Withdrawal/avoidance impulses (e.g. wanting to drop out)
antecedent: Starting to learn more complex math content at the beginning of the term
target_behavior.core_reason: Long-standing math weakness and catastrophic interpretation of failure; comparison with past grades reinforcing the 'I am not smart enough' core belief, triggering failure Anticipation and shame Fear
target_behavior.function: Escaping in the short term the shame and Anxiety brought by being evaluated and failing
target_behavior.consequence: Declining academic performance, overall grades affected; Relationship tension with classmates; Sleep and appetite affected

target_behavior.behavior: Mind going blank and impaired attention in exams, with 'I will fail' automatic thoughts
antecedent: Entering a high-stakes exam for a difficult course
Negative Anticipation about one's abilities and outcomes
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong Anxiety and negative Automatic thoughts occupying working memory, creating a vicious physiological-cognitive cycle
target_behavior.function: Reducing the mental load when facing difficult questions in the short term (maladaptive response)
target_behavior.consequence: Exam performance impaired, frustration intensifies, further consolidating failure beliefs
